label: copy output e is near (output window around an e), and e-initial sequences approaching <DEL>
explanation: Letter-e output feature. In the copy phase it fires in a window around the step that outputs an original e: the step before (next_out == e, ~75% rate), the e-output step itself (92% rate, 13.8x lift), and the step after, where e comes back as input and activation is smaller. If e is among the first original tokens (orig(0) or orig(1)), it also builds up through the late original phase from t>=3 and peaks at <DEL>, just before e has to be emitted. That covers the top activations, e.g. e e e x y <DEL> -> ~1.0 at <DEL>. Magnitude is largest when the e comes early (orig(0)) and in sequences with repeated e, and it ramps up over the original phase toward <DEL>. It never fires at t=0-1 and is almost silent at t=2. It is weak and rare for outputs other than e; w/z/x/t outputs show 2-2.6x lift, which is probably mild cross-talk. Unexplained: a diffuse low-magnitude background (~0.1 relative) around <DEL> and early copy steps in sequences with no e, which accounts for most of the missed activations. Most false positives are near-threshold e-window steps.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=e (+5.54), out_tok=e (+5.36), next_out=e (+5.08), orig1=e (+4.42), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+4.25), phase=2 & out_tok=e (+3.76). Lower it: phase=2 & in_tok=i (-10.98), phase=2 & in_tok=p (-10.09), out_tok=i (-8.46), out_tok=p (-7.61).
